 Pop Culture News Kylie Jenner’s ex-housekeeper says she was locked in closet, bitten by dog and pepper-sprayed working for her
 The allegations appear in the latest lawsuit against Jenner, 29, who has now been sued by four former staffers within the last seven months. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Kylie Jenner at the 2025 Met Gala in New York City. Dia Dipasupil / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 11, 2026, 11:54 AM EST  /  Updated   Nov. 11, 2026, 12:38 PM EST By Matt Lavietes Kylie Jenner’s former housekeeper is suing the reality star and cosmetics mogul, alleging she was trapped inside Jenner’s closet, bitten by a dog and accidentally pepper-sprayed in the face.
 The lawsuit is the fourth against Jenner, the 29-year-old co-star of “The Kardashians” and founder of Kylie Cosmetics, by members of her household staff in the last seven months. 
 Dinora Carolina Cabria Amaya filed the lawsuit in Los Angeles County Superior Court on Nov. 5, accusing Jenner, her company and two members of her staff — Laura Dooley and Itzel Sibrian — of disability discrimination, retaliation, wrongful termination and numerous labor violations. 
 Amaya worked at several of Jenner’s California residences from March 2025 until she was fired in February, according to the complaint. She earned $40 an hour — roughly $23 above the state’s minimum wage — and worked six days a week. Jenner owns several multimillion-dollar properties in the Los Angeles area, in addition to a La Quinta mansion outside Palm Springs. 
 Amaya alleges that on an unspecified date, she became locked inside Jenner’s closet and “confined against her will.” The complaint says that Dooley instructed her to enter the closet and gave her the passcode but that she became locked inside.
 When she became trapped, Amaya called Dooley, who “laughed and mocked her” and “refused to disclose the access information necessary to obtain her release,” according to the lawsuit. Amaya alleged she had a panic attack and was trapped in the closet for more than an hour. 
 On Sept. 4, 2025, while Amaya was cleaning and organizing a drawer in one of Jenner’s laundry rooms, an unsecured canister of pepper spray discharged directly into her eyes and face, the lawsuit alleges. The more she “complained that she was hurt, the harder Defendants made her job,” removing other staffers who had been helping her and requiring her to complete work alone, according to the complaint.
 On Oct. 28, 2025, Amaya was assigned to clean a doghouse, according to the complaint. While she was performing the assigned work, a dog bit her, according to the suit. The lawsuit does not state whom the dog belonged to. Jenner has owned several dogs since she was a teenager, some of them being prominently featured on her family’s former reality show “Keeping Up With the Kardashians.”
 Amaya alleged that after she complained about her injuries, Jenner’s staff “increased her workload, assigned heavier tasks, and abruptly changed her schedule and work locations.”
 “Defendants were making her life miserable so she would quit,” the lawsuit says.
 Michael Rhodes, a lawyer for Jenner, noted in a statement that the four cases against his client were being brought by the same attorney.
 “It’s clear that this lawyer wants to use publicity to try and extract an unwarranted payday. We’re not going to be intimidated into doing that,” Rhodes said. “As such, we’ll defend these meritless cases vigorously and look forward to telling our side of the story.”

 Slide 1 of 1 “We came prepared with evidence, not publicity stunts,” she said. “Attempts to intimidate and silence my clients may have worked before they had someone willing to stand up for them. Those days are over.”
 Sibrian declined to comment. A woman who answered a phone number associated with Dooley hung up when she was asked about her employment.
 Jenner was first sued by former members of her staff in April, when another former housekeeper, Angelica Hernandez Vasquez, alleged that she had been discriminated against. 
 Vasquez alleged that she was “mocked for accent and treated as inferior because of her Salvadoran background” and discriminated against for being Catholic. Vasquez in addition accused one of her supervisors of throwing a clothing hanger at her feet while reprimanding her.
 Later that month, Juana Delgado Soto sued Jenner alleging that she endured years of discrimination, humiliation and wage violations while she was working as a housekeeper for more than six years. 
 And in June, a private chef who worked for Jenner alleged that she suffered a miscarriage in February 2025 while she was working for Jenner. 
 The chef, who is identified only as Jane Doe, was under “overwhelming physical strain” while she was working at a birthday party for Jenner’s child in Palm Springs on Feb. 1, 2025, according to the lawsuit. Her “requests for assistance were dismissed” and met with “hostility,” the lawsuit alleges.
 The next day, the chef woke up to severe hemorrhaging and lost her unborn child, the lawsuit says. She was five months pregnant. She alleged that she was fired in late March, weeks after she returned from medical leave for the miscarriage.
